utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (No translation) (The accused/witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Generally, Mr. President, we'd like to tell our client if he's going to be the subject of photography in the morning. We'd just like to tell him so he's not surprised or disturbed by something unexpected. We would make that request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: First, the Registrar or, rather, the Presiding Judge and the other Judges were informed that the photographer would be here, and the Registrar is the one who had raised the issue. In any case, in all good faith I thought that the Defence counsel and the Prosecution counsel had been alerted. You know, this is a public hearing, and I can't see any base objection. However, in the future we will inform you, Mr. Hayman. Do you have any other comments that you'd like to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: No, we'd just like to be able to tell him so he won't be concerned that this is something unusual or triggered by some other event he may be unaware of, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I find that to be a reasonable request. The witness is in a difficult position because he is now testifying. We will consider your request and proceed differently. All right. We don't have to say anything further about that. I would like now to say good morning to the interpreters. I didn't have time to say good morning, but I heard Mr. Hayman, therefore, I thought that all of the booths were working properly, and I thought that by saying good -- I would like to ask the witness to tell us whether he has not been disturbed but, you know, there are photographers that want to come in some times. Let me remind you that the ICTY was established by the International Community so that it be a public institution and the hearings are public. Nonetheless, I would turn to the witness and ask him a question. You were too disturbed by that, General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think, therefore, that your Defence counsel was more disturbed than you were then.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I was a bit surprised because I didn't know in advance that it would happen, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I thought that you were just going to tell me now that you were going to agree with your counsel but, all right. It doesn't matter. We can now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, good morning Your Honours. Good morning counsel, good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Kehoe:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, we'd like to move back to where we left off yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I would look at 406/46 and 406/31 [real-time transcript read 206/46 and 206/31 in error]. It says 206. It should be 406, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The transcript says 206 and Mr. Harmon points out it should be 406/46 and 406/31.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: These are Prosecution Exhibits; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, 406/26 is the order that you gave out on the 5th of October of 1992 to all the municipal headquarters --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. The document that we're looking at right now is 406/26.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document 406/26 that is on the ELMO now, that is in your hands, General, is the order that you gave on the 5th of October, 1992 to all the municipal headquarters asking for an urgent submission on HV officers in your unit. In response to that you said there were no HV officers in Central Bosnia. Now, let us turn to the next Exhibit which is 406/31, an order dated the 26th of November, 1992 from the Zenica command. Now, you're familiar with this document, General. Is the Zenica command within the Central Bosnia Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is, but, Your Honours, I apologise, perhaps I didn't get the right interpretation, so may I repeat? The translation I heard was that with the document 406/26, I asked for the urgent deployment of HV units in the HVO of Central Bosnia. In this document 406/26, I didn't ask for the urgent deployment of HV units into the HVO of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There must have been a translation problem, General. The question was urgent information concerning HV officers in your area. That is what the order asked for, urgent information concerning those people, to which you testified yesterday there were none.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. HV officers or HV soldiers did not exist in the HVO of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to 406/31, which is the order of 26 November, 1992 from the Zenica command, specifically the deputy commander of the Zenica command Zoran Covic. You just noted that the Zenica command is within the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Is it not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Covic is one of your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In point 3 of this particular document it notes that: "HV Croatian army members present in this region and wearing HV insignia must be warned to take them off as this creates trouble for the Republic Croatia." Now, quite clearly, Mr. Covic notes HV members in this region and the region he's talking about is the Zenica region; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could allow the witness a few minutes to read the document. He didn't write that document, it is not his document, so he should be given a little time to read through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President. This document came into evidence about a year and a half ago, and I think if we move things along the question should be asked of this particular witness whether or not over the last year and a half he has had the opportunity to review these documents. I can give the specific date when Mr. Cayley introduced this into evidence, but I submit to the Court it is approximately a year and a half ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me turn to the witness. Have you had the opportunity to look at this document again with your counsel?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: With my attorneys I did not see this document, but I did see the document in the courtroom during the proceedings, but I read it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But the counsel has read that, hasn't he, or reread that? Counsel has read it? No?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. President, but we are not testifying. We can tell you everything about that document but we are not testifying. It is a matter for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I wasn't asking such a naive question as you might assume. I want to know what the connection was between the witness and his counsel so that we don't spend all our time reading documents, but we have to make sure that the accused's rights are maintained. I was not asking such a naive question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: There are tens of thousands of pages of documents that have been introduced, Mr. President, and something that may have been put on the ELMO a year and a half ago does not deprive the witness the right, I think, to review a document if he needs to so he can answer questions precisely and accurately. That's all we maintain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you're never going to make me fall into that kind of a configuration. I would not take any rights away from the accused at all. Let me remind you that the accused today is testifying as a witness. He has all the rights of a witness in addition to all the rights of the accused, but he does not have any more rights than any other witness. We have to try to manage our time properly. When we're speaking about a short document, I believe that the witness can familiarise himself quickly with that document but all the more so because I had asked the Prosecutor to focus his questions. I have to say that Mr. Kehoe is doing just that. For once, Mr. Kehoe is listening to what I'm asking him to do. I can't give him any further orders, but it's a very simple question. Let's not exaggerate. A very simple question. This was an order Mr. Kehoe explained very quickly and it focuses the question on point 3. It was very simple, I think. I think for a witness like yours, that is, a witness who isn't someone who is illiterate but rather someone who is very quick-witted, he can understand the question, and I will not accept our spending too much time reading and moving documents about, otherwise, Mr. Hayman, we're going to celebrate Christmas here together concerning the Blaskic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We're not asking for too much time, but counsel is asking to deviate from the procedures that the Court has laid down. I was responding to counsel's proposal. I support the Court's practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. There's nothing further to say about this now. I suppose in the meantime, General Blaskic has been able to familiarise himself with the document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Question then, please, on point 3. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, when Mr. Covic is talking about HV members present in this region, he is talking about the Zenica region which was within the Central Bosnia Operative Zone; isn't he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From this order it would indicate that Mr. Covic believes that there are HV members in the Zenica area?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know very well that in the Operative Zone of the HVO of Central Bosnia there were no members of the Croatian army ever, and that they frequently received the same orders as they're addressed to commanders of the Operative Zone of North-western Herzegovina and Southeast Herzegovina, to check whether any Croatian army members were present. Therefore, this order is based on an order of the HVO main staff which sent the same orders to me and Commander Siljeg in the form of a circular in the Operative Zone of North-western Herzegovina, so that this order was simply copied.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, did you know about this order being issued on the 26th of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that we frequently did checks of this kind. I can't say precisely regarding this date. I do know Covic. He was a taxi driver before he joined the HVO; he has no military training, therefore; and he simply copied those orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you issue an order to the brigades and the independent units concerning the subject matter addressed in Covic's order, i.e. the HV wearing HV patches in Central Bosnia? Did you issue such an order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Croatian army -- let me repeat. You asked me whether I issued an order about the Croatian army wearing Croatian army insignia. That is the question that I got. I did not issue an order about the Croatian army wearing HV insignia because there were no such troops in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from your testimony, would you conclude that Covic wrote this order on his own without any instructions from the command of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Covic certainly received an order to verify, and he must have received such an order from the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and I believe -- there is no number here -- but I believe that he simply copied out this order, that such an order had arrived in Central Bosnia, just as it must have gone to Herzegovina, issued by the main staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in fact, when it came from the main staff, you issued an order and Covic responded to that order; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My command issued it. I am not sure that it was me personally because I was in Travnik in the joint command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like a clarification, General Blaskic. In respect of yourself, who was Covic in that structure?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, he was deputy commander of the staff in Zenica, the headquarters in Zenica, deputy commander of the municipal staff in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: At that point, you were what?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, I had my forward command post in Travnik, and that is where I was in charge of the defence of Travnik with some of my associates, whereas the administrative offices of the command were still in the hotel in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, when you say your command issued an order to the brigades, did they issue that order with your knowledge and approval?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you explain or did your command explain to the brigades the problems that it was creating for the Republic of Croatia, to have HV members wearing HV insignia in the Central Bosnian Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I repeat. There were no members of the Croatian army in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, but there were HVO members wearing different insignia, including HVO and the HV, and here, in document 406/31, it is stated that there were insignia associated with the Ustashe and fascist movement. This was a time when the HVO were in the process of being established. Some members would wear village insignia even. So there were various markings being used, and Commander Covic says, "In order to eliminate this in the future and in order that HVO members should wear the same insignia, I order ..." And this order consists of five points, and I believe that it was literally copied out from the command of the Operative Zone which, in turn, copied it out from an order received from the main staff because the main staff would send to all Operative Zones the same command. If 406/26 had been received from the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, I don't think that it would have issued such an order to the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to another exhibit and another area of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and I would ask Mr. Usher for 406/36.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, have you seen this before? If you have seen it before, we can move through it quickly.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen it, but allow me a moment to read it. I am familiar with the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, General. This is a document that was signed by Mr. Ivan Primorac, we have heard of before, the commander of the 3rd HVO Brigade in the Mostar area, 9 December, 1992, and it responds to an order issued by the Southeast Herzegovina Operative Zone of 27 November, 1992. At that time, who was the commanding officer of the Southeast Herzegovina Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I know that the commander of the Operative Zone of South-eastern Herzegovina was Colonel Mica Lasic, but I'm not sure that he was the commander in that period. On that date, whether he was in command or not, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perfectly okay, General, if you don't recall. That is fine. Let us move through this document. Regarding this order coming from the commander "regarding various insignia and symbols on HVO uniforms worn as opposed to the symbols stipulated by the Decree on Herceg-Bosna Armed Forces which, as such, compromise the reputation of HVO and HV members by implying ideas which the world media may interpret as fascistic, I hereby order ..." Now, in the order that you got from the main command on this subject, did the main staff indicate that the media was talking about fascistic ideas; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is hard for me to recall that now, but possibly it did because this order from the command of South-eastern Herzegovina has virtually the same heading and preamble as Zoran Covic's order that we were examining a moment ago. So that clearly the main command, as I said, sent out circular orders regarding the same issue. When I say "issued," I meant to all the Operative Zones without taking into consideration the reports received from the Operative Zones regarding that problem, because if it had, there would have been no need to issue such an order to the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the main staff was issuing orders to the Operative Zones knowing that they were going to get back information that there were no HV members, at least in your Operative Zone; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. What I'm trying to say is that the main command sent orders to all the zones without taking into consideration reports received from us. So that if, even though they had a report saying that there were no HV members, clearly the main command issued an order to South-eastern Herzegovina and Central Bosnia regarding insignia covering all the issues consisting of six items in document 406/36.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, at this time, when the Covic order goes out and during the time frame when the Primorac order goes out, were you aware that the presence and the allegations of the presence of HV troops in Bosnia-Herzegovina was causing problems for the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the period of November and December, I claim with full responsibility that I was in Travnik, and I didn't know whether we would be able to hold on to Travnik or not, and there I had meetings with UNPROFOR officers, I went to the feature called Mescema on the first front lines, and the only thing I remember -- I was not aware of what you are asking me about. The only thing I was aware of was the need to defend the town of Travnik and hold onto it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when Covic wrote in his order of 406/31 that the wearing of HVO insignia -- HV insignia creates trouble for the people of Croatia, you don't know anything about that; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Asked and answered, Mr. President. Counsel is arguing with the witness. The witness is perfectly clear on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, there was no answer. I'm sorry, Mr. Hayman, but there was no answer to the question. This is a different question now. Up to this point, the witness said that he -- well, that either orders were re-copied or that HV soldiers were not in his command area. It is an old answer and we are taking note of it. But the witness also said that general circulars were issued in that way by the central headquarters to all the command areas, which was his own. Now this is a different question. And the third answer of your witness was to say that frequently the orders were re-copied. I have the impression that many things were re-copied at that point. I think there is a lot of copying work going on. But anyway, that doesn't matter. There were three types of answers that the witness gave. The question now is additional, saying, "All right, very well. You were re-copying things. There was no HV in your command zone. That's fine. Now the question is: Did you know that there were possibly HV soldiers when you read those circulars?" And the witness could say that he didn't even read the circulars. That's possible. But we are going to hear his answer. Therefore, I consider that the answer was not given, and I will ask the Prosecutor to ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, my question is this: Were you aware that the allegations that soldiers had HV insignia, that allegation by the International Community was causing problems for the Republic of Croatia? Did you understand my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That soldiers wearing Croatian army insignia were causing problems for the Republic of Croatia? Was that your question? I didn't quite get it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the translation I got doesn't have any meaning. The question, the way I understood it, and it was in the same language as the witness, whether soldiers bearing Croatian army insignia were causing difficulties for the Republic of Croatia. Of course, the Croatian army has all soldiers with HV insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: [interpretation cuts in] ... question. See if there's an interpretation -- Croatian. General Blaskic, do you know whether at that point there were allegations that the presence of Croatian army soldiers could create problems for the Republic of Croatia? That's the question. Do you understand me, what I'm saying to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am familiar with this order that I received from the main command and I know that something like that was said in the preamble.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Firstly I am asking whether you understood my question, and we will see whether the interpreters are operating properly. It is a very simple question. I ask the question: Did you know that there were allegations circulating according to which the presence of soldiers wearing Croatian uniforms might cause problems for the Republic of Croatia? Has my question been properly interpreted? What did you understand in my question? I'm going to get to the very end of this issue of interpretation. We are not going to go all the way to July speaking about interpretation problems. I am prepared to be sure that there is disciplined interpretation, but we have to know what we're talking about. What did you understand as the question?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Whether I knew that allegations on the presence of Croatian soldiers in Bosnia-Herzegovina were causing difficulties for the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like to thank the interpreters who are doing their work properly. All right. Now, please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew about that on the basis of the orders I was receiving from the main HVO staff, but that was not my main concern in my work in Central Bosnia because I knew that there were no such soldiers there at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Judge Rodrigues would like to ask a question. Thank you. That is the type of coherent answer, and it's your answer, and it will be noted as such. Judge Rodrigues. Excuse me, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, I have a question I'd like to ask and here it is: Do you have in front of you the two documents that we are dealing with now?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have document /36 in front of me now, 406/36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: So it's the document which was signed by Mr. Primarac; is that correct? In the original -- do you have the original? I mean, the original in Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have the original, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: What does it say under point 5?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not have point 5. I have 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: All right. Point 5 is missing.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Point 5 is missing on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: This is my question: As Judge Jorda said, there was a lot of work being done by people copying things. The individual who issued the order, understanding that he would not be able to verify the actual situation in order to respond to the questions asked about the order that had been received, did he merely not answer? I can ask my question a different way. I'll do that. Did those people who were supposed to respond to an order for information -- they didn't have any information and, therefore, did not refer to this number. Could one think that way? Because, as you said -- I don't know what Mr. Primorac's training was, but the other deputy was a taxi driver and, therefore, the person could have thought, "I don't have any information. Therefore, I won't answer."

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a document from the Operative Zone of Southeast Herzegovina, Mostar, Capljina, Stolac. Therefore, it is not the Central Bosnia area. I don't know what the situation was like then in Mostar. This is the 3rd Brigade, which was in Mostar. Quite possibly at that time there was some Croatian army there with them, because it is the southern part towards Neum, Ploce, Stolac, and Capljina, but what I was talking about is that the same order was received for the whole of Herceg-Bosna, which means the main staff sent a circular order, the same orders for this check to be undertaken. That is why I said that probably in these frequent checks that were made the main staff did not always check the information from the Operative Zones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, now we get to the very heart of the issue. There was a general situation in Mostar and information was being asked from all the different zones, but it might happen that in one zone the information was not available but that information might exist in another zone, and the zone where there was no information didn't respond, was simply -- not put anything in. Instead of saying about point 5, "I have no information," and simply saying nothing. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We always checked orders of this kind. So regardless of whether I have or do not have them, I copy out the order and perform a check because it is an enormous area and various things can happen. So all the reports that I received back to me I send on to the main staff. The problem is, and I believe that the problem was, whether the main staff exercised checks of this kind vis-à-vis the reports that it received from the Operative Zones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, imagine or let's say that from the main staff you received an order asking you for information about whether there were HV soldiers in your zone. You are a person, as the presiding Judge has already said, who is extremely intelligent, and you could answer by saying, "I don't have information that I can give you because the situation has not been checked." Perhaps you provide that, but the taxi driver, who does not have your kind of background, your kind of training, could that taxi driver admit or could he not admit that type of information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the latter half of your question. Can the taxi driver omit that type of information, omit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Instead of saying, I "don't have information" -- under point 5, instead of saying, "I don't have information to give you," you, who having the kind of training that you have, I assume that you can answer that way, but is it possible that a taxi driver, faced with the situation, could answer by saying nothing at all, that is, not answer, say nothing? Point 5. That he could simply draw a line, leave it blank. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never, or it was not standard practice to proceed in that way and say that in my zone there were no such soldiers, for the simple reason that the zone is such a large one that during my entire service I was never able to tour it all, unfortunately. What I did was that my associates, the administrative personnel that I had, would copy out the order and send it to all the municipal staff. Then the municipal staff would copy out the same thing once again, either in the form of an order or in the form of the report, and send it back once they had checked it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in response to a question of Judge Rodrigues, you noted that in December of 1992 when Primorac wrote this order 406/36, that quite possibly HVO soldiers may have been in the Mostar area -- excuse me, HV soldiers were in the Mostar area. Do you recall saying that to Judge Rodrigues?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That it was possible that they were in that area. Perhaps they were. I wasn't in that area. That is why I say, I don't see any logic as to why checks should be carried out as to the presence of the Croatian army unless they were somewhere within the totality of the community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were they there, sir? Were there HV soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you're asking me personally, I personally did not see them and I do not have any direct information as to whether they were or were not. I personally did not see them, but I heard that -- rumours were going around that there was this presence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who did you learn this from, that there were HV soldiers in the Mostar area?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were various talks with international officers, officers of UNPROFOR. For example, they asked me whether aid would be sent from the Croatian army to Central Bosnia. I remember very well on one occasion I was asked by one of the commanders of the UNPROFOR battalion in 1993, then there was information broadcast over the radio that there were members of the Croatian army, and I was informed of this by the system for information but, as I say, I personally never saw them and I never talked to those members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in your struggles, General, would HV soldiers and the deployment of HV soldiers to your area have helped your situation?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Soldiers of the Croatian army in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, they did not exist there, but of every soldier who wanted to include himself into the defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time, and we're talking about 1992, November or December of 1992, would have been welcome for help and assistance. Any help to the defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina would have been welcomed. So any volunteer, as I say, would have been welcomed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, when you learned from the international sources as well as media sources that there were HV troops around Mostar, did you discuss that matter with the main staff, with the hope that they would send those troops up to Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I personally do not recall that I had talks of that kind, because the situation was as it was since January 1993, that is to say, the area of Central Bosnia was isolated in terms of communication, and I can't see where they could have sent them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, at the time this order was issued, General Praljak seemed to be present on several occasions in Central Bosnia. Did you discuss with General Praljak, an HV General, the possibility of sending HV troops to Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: General Praljak went for management purposes to the explosives factory to talk to the directors there. As I said, he was there on two or three occasions, but I did not discuss this matter with him. I think that it was matters of the joint command that talked to him, particularly with regard to matters of ammunition and defence for the defence of Travnik in that period. That was our priority at the time, and the defence went from the joint command of the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, let us address ourselves back to Exhibit 406/36, and the issue that I would want to discuss with you is point 3, wherein that Mr. Primorac writes: "Wearing HVO insignia is linked to accusations against the Republic of Croatia, and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna regarding a direct deployment of HV units in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Ask HV members (with explanation) to wear HVO insignia during their employment (sic) in the area." Now, my question for you, General, is this order orders that HV troops be disguised as HVO troops; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Once again, I did not receive the interpretation as it is written in what I have here.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, the B/C/S booth doesn't have a copy of the original B/C/S text and this is causing problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We have an objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The translation was "employment."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman is right. It should be "deployment" to the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this particular order -- I'm sorry, Judge. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this order by Mr. Primorac orders that HV members disguise themselves, with an explanation, by wearing HVO insignia; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, what order are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President. We're talking about order 406/36, and the point of reference is point 3. Paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. 406, paragraph 36 (sic), paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I understand this order as it is stated in point 3, that during the time they spend on our territory, the members of the HV should wear insignia of the HVO and the area is Mostar. The date is on the 9th, '92. That is to say, during their stay there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you, General, is with an explanation. This order orders HV troops deployed to the area to disguise themselves as HVO troops by changing the shoulder patch; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I cannot see from this point here that the order is to issue orders to the Croatian army to deploy in this territory, but they are asked during the time they spend in that territory that they wear the HVO insignia in the Mostar region, while they are in the Mostar area. But it does not order that Croatian army troops be deployed in the area in point 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, I would like to give the floor to Judge Shahabuddeen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, would you say that paragraph 3 of this order was concerned only with the wearing of emblems? Did it say that HV troops should not be in the area or did it say that any HV troops in the area should wear HVO insignia? Look at the last two lines of paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, in point 3, I understand point 3 to mean the following, that it is asked that HVO insignia be worn by individuals so as to avoid accusations about the direct engagement of the HV in the Herceg-Bosna region, and in the last section, it asks the HV members, during their stay in the region, to wear HVO insignia. I said that there were situations where the members of the HV, and if I may, I can quote examples, can go on leave because they signed a professional contract with the Croatian army, and so during their sojourn in Bosnia-Herzegovina, while they are on leave, they perhaps wear HV insignia. I did not talk to Mr. Primorac about point 3 or about this document at all. But it is clearly stated here, members of the HV, during their sojourn in our area. Now, why they are in that area -- were they included into combat operations? It is in December 1992, and as far as I know, in December '92, that was the time when the HVO and the BH army acted together. It was the time when we had our best cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Let me follow that up by asking this question: Did the arrangements mean that any HV soldiers would continue to be HV soldiers subject to their wearing HVO insignia or did the arrangements mean that any HV soldiers in the area would become HVO soldiers upon wearing HVO insignia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I personally can say what I believe with respect to the time period in question and my comment on it. Every soldier of the HV who, for any reason, that is to say, individual, found himself on the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, according to this particular point, should have placed the HVO insignia on, if he had gone to visit his family, for example, or to visit his wife or parents or generally if he was present on the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Because it says here "Ask" them, "Ask" them. Had it been a question of the army, the words would have been "Order" them, but it says "Ask HVO members (with explanation), during their deployment in our area, to wear HVO insignia," if they were on leave and came to the territory of Herceg-Bosna at that particular time, if they were present in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, I know that any HV soldiers deployed in the area were required to wear HVO insignia. What I am asking is this: Would such an HV soldier remain an HV soldier even during the period when he was wearing HVO insignia or would such an HV soldier be transformed into an HVO soldier during the period when he was wearing HVO insignia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can comment on the question. Because I do not have certain information on that, I can just give my comment. I think that a soldier wearing HVO insignia would be an HVO soldier and had there been units engaged -- I said that I heard rumours about that but not first-hand, I didn't hear this information first-hand, about HV units on this territory. We looked at this at different time periods, and mentioned this yesterday, with the different tasks and assignments involved. At one time it was to prevent an occupation of Bosnia-Herzegovina; another time, unfortunately, it was a time when there were conflicts between what were allies, between the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So if such an HV soldier were to become an HVO soldier during the period when he was wearing HVO insignia, would that help you to answer Mr. Kehoe's question as to whether such an HV soldier was disguising himself as an HVO soldier?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If such a soldier had been demobilised, Your Honours, in the Croatian army, and received documents that his active duty in the Croatian army had been terminated, and, to give an example, if he was going back to his native village and would go there to contact the competent authorities of National Defence and informs that active service had been discontinued and if he receives a new war assignment within some HVO unit, then, for me, that soldier would be an HVO soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: If that HV soldier was not demobilised within the Croatian army, would I be right in supposing that that HV soldier would continue to be an HV soldier during the period when he was wearing HVO insignia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course. If he had not been demobilised in the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I have an explanation or clarification I would like to give you. Still talking about point 3 of 406/36. Can one deduce from this order that comes from Mr. Primorac, who is an important person, can we deduce that the direct deployment of units from Croatia existed, in fact?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would just like to emphasise that it is difficult for me to conclude something of the kind if I read this document and which says, "Ask HV members (with explanation) to wear HVO insignia during their deployment in our area." I would say, "Ask a soldier while executing assignments in the area," and I wouldn't say "Ask," I wouldn't use the word "Ask."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I am asking you to listen to my question very carefully. When a very high-ranking soldier -- I am going to speak slowly so there is no interpretation problem. When he takes the trouble to put in point 3 the sentence saying that HVO insignia is linked to accusations against the Republic of Croatia and the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna regarding direct deployment of HV units, could that be read or interpreted as meaning that the direct deployment, in fact, existed, that there was direct deployment? Can it be read that way? I am not saying whether you read it that way, but could it be read that way? Could it be read that way?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It could be read in that way, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me give you an example, a metaphor. If, within this Trial Chamber, I were to read one evening, "Be careful or take care of the model here," could that be interpreted as meaning that the model, in fact, was in the courtroom? You understand my question? I'm not asking whether you agree, whether you agree about the substance, I simply want to know whether one could conclude that from having read the sentence? When I say to the security service, "Be careful not to photograph the accused very early in the morning," could one then assume that there would be a photographer? It is a semantic issue. Do you understand what I'm asking you? Could it be read that way, that there was direct HV deployment? I'm not talking about Mr. Covic. The taxi driver didn't sign. It was a very high-ranking individual who did. Could it be read that way?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, the direct engagement existed in 1992. We saw that yesterday looking through many of the documents. But we are talking about December 1992; and when I look at that date, I am trying to remember the circumstances as far as I knew them, what they were at the time, and that is why I said that it was a time when we had ideal cooperation between the two commands, between the HVO and the BH army, in the fight against the army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In other words, you are saying that it could be read that way but that, in fact, there was no direct deployment in December 1992? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I personally did not see nor did I have direct knowledge on this. Possibly there could have been. It is possible that there was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. It's possible that there was. You see, it was a bit long, but we got to the answer; that is, it could be read that way. Therefore, my comment is the following: If we start by saying that there was direct deployment or that there could have been direct deployment, at that point we understand the last sentence very clearly. That means that we have to ask the HV members to wear the HVO insignia. But this is only one interpretation given by a humble judge from the International Criminal Tribunal who perhaps went too far and who also needs a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will now resume the hearing. Please be seated. Excuse me, Mr. Kehoe, but Judge Shahabuddeen would like to ask a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, I want to return to the questions I was putting to you and to conclude the line of inquiry which was asking this: Were the new arrangements which required HV soldiers to wear HVO insignia to take effect automatically and immediately?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not familiar in the way in which this took place and what kind of arrangements were made, but I could assume -- I can only express my views or understanding, and that would be that a commander would issue orders to a unit to attach other insignia, but I do not know. I have no information as to how this took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would you be able to tell us whether all HV soldiers were demobilised from the Croatian army before they started to wear HVO insignia or whether it was the case that some HV soldiers continued to be in the Croatian army after they began to wear HVO insignia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that quite a number of soldiers of the Croatian army who had been terminated in the Croatian army on various grounds, who were demobilised, who returned to Bosnia-Herzegovina and were then mobilised to the HVO or the BH army. So that applied to one group of those soldiers or individuals. I also believe that there were some soldiers, possibly even smaller units, which wore HVO insignia and were actually in the HV but there were no such soldiers in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. My belief is based on what I heard but not from any direct knowledge that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: General, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those soldiers that you just talked about that were in the HV but were wearing HVO insignia were soldiers that were trying to disguise their true identity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Such individuals probably tried to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a common practice in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was not the practice in the HVO, if you're referring to '92 and '93, in the area where I was. I can only speak about that area. As to what was happening in South-eastern Herzegovina at the time, I don't know because I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, one last question on 406/36 in paragraph 3. The word "deployment" is used twice, the direct employment of HV units and talking about HV members during their deployment. In your military lexicon, what is the definition of the word "deployment"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In point 3, in the Croatian language, in the text before me, it says: "Is linked to accusations about the direct engagement of HV units," but then further on did says: "Members of the HV should be asked (with explanation) during their stay in our area to wear HVO insignia." I have already said that reference is made to members of the HV, individuals who are to be asked, while staying in this area, to wear HVO insignia. As a soldier, I don't understand why the order "order" is not used. Secondly, when it says, "Members of the HV," it doesn't say "HV units."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could have the witness take a look at 406/10 and then 406/54. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, for reference purposes, General, in 406/10, this is the order we discussed yesterday, that General Bobetko gives order to, in number 2, Zeljko Siljeg. Now, Mr. Siljeg ultimately became the commander of the Northwest Herzegovina Operative Zone as we can see in 406/54; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. In the document dated 12 April, 1993, the commander of the Operative Zone of North-western Herzegovina is Zeljko Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this order by Siljeg on the 12th of April, 1993, we no longer have a problem with insignia but this letter coming from the main staff asks for records and defining the status of HV officers in the HVO. Pursuant to that he issues the order: "Submit a list of all HV officers present in your units and the headquarters." In number 2, Siljeg wants the father's name, last name and, "submit the orders which authorised his referral to the HVO, rank and no. of decree of promotion (reserve and career) and the duty he is currently carrying out in your army and the duties he has carried out so far." Now, this particular document references in number 2 references two. It says: "The orders which authorise the HV officer's referral to the HVO." Now who would execute that order, the HV or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My understanding of this order is that it would be issued in the HV, that is, an order terminating active military service, and then officers with complete files would move to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This next comment that it says: "The number of decree of promotion." Is that, likewise, an HV document or is that an HVO document?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When you request termination of service, and if you have a particular rank, then the rank would be indicated and everything else. That is my assumption. Then that person would go to the new command and report to the new command with all these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, how far is Gornji Vakuf away from Vitez and your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number of kilometres, because there was no road before the war between Gornji Vakuf and Vitez, there was just a mountain pass. The road was built during the war. I think it is about an hour's drive along that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the conflict that was taking place in Gornji Vakuf in January of 1993, you were getting daily situation reports or routine situation reports from Gornji Vakuf as to what was happening; weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would occasionally get reports. They were not daily, but I would get reports about what was happening, as many as I could get, since this was the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps of Bosnia-Herzegovina which had its own command in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this conflict with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in January of 1993, Siljeg was the commander of the Northwest Herzegovina Operative Zone; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. The translation was wrong. So now I understand. Yes. As far as I know, Siljeg was the commander of the Operative Zone of North-western Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Siljeg have HV troops fighting with him against the Muslims during this January conflict?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about that, whether he had or did not have any Croatian army forces. I have no direct knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss it with him?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: With him personally? I did not, as far as I can recollect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you became the deputy chief of staff or the chief of staff of the HVO, did you learn that there had been HV troops fighting with the HV in Gornji Vakuf against the Muslims in January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I learned that there were individuals. We didn't specify the time, was it January or sometime later but, as far as I can recollect, it was a unit consisting of Croats who were by birth from Bosnia-Herzegovina. Whether it was a battalion or the 175th Brigade I don't know, but I know that there were such cases and we did discuss this later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, General, there were, in fact, HV troops fighting with the HVO in Gornji Vakuf against the Muslims in January of 1993; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am not looking at the transcript, and I don't understand it anyway, but let me repeat your question. There were HV troops fighting with the HVO in January '93 against the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were conflicts between the HVO and the BH army in January 1993 in Gornji Vakuf. I think the translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: A double mistake in the translation. The translation of what Mr. Kehoe said was wrong because the translation was that HVO and HVO troops were fighting in Gornji Vakuf, and then when the witness wanted to check that question and repeated it, then the English translation was misinterpreted as if the witness has asked whether HV and HVO troops were fighting together. So we had a double error, first from English into B/C/S and then from B/C/S into English. Mr. Kehoe's question was whether HV and HVO troops were fighting in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we are waiting for this document, General, the Ante Starcevic Brigade is part of the Northwest Herzegovina Operative Zone, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 600 and 600A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is no French copy of this as yet, so I will put it on the ELMO and read it slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This comes from Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade in Gornji Vakuf. The date is 22 February, 1993. It goes to the 4th Split Brigade, Drazevac Barracks, Split. Ms. Dragica Hamer. Pardon my pronunciation. Now, the 4th Split Brigade, General, is an HV brigade [real-time transcript read "HVO" in error], isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the 4th Split Brigade is a brigade of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It reads as follows: "Further to your inquiry regarding the death of your combatant, Stanko Posavac, son of Frano, from Gornji Vakuf, it was established that Stanko Posavac took part in the fighting between the so-called BH Army and the HVO in Gornji Vakuf and was wounded by a sniper bullet on 13 January 1993 at M. Tita Street /no number/ in Gornji Vakuf. He was transferred the same day to the Firule Hospital in Split where he died between 1700 and 1800 hours on 25 January, 1993. For reasons of security, he was buried at the Paloc local cemetery at 1800 hours on 27 January, 1993." Do you recognise that stamp, General?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Kehoe. I want to stop for a moment here because we have the English transcript in front of us. On line 17, you asked: "The 4th Split Brigade is an HVO brigade, isn't it?" Answer: "Yes, it is a brigade of the Croatian army."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Judge. The question should have been: Was the 4th Split Brigade an HV brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. But in the transcript, it is "HVO."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could correct that? Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 4th Split Brigade is an HV brigade, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you recognise this stamp and do you know Mr. Tokic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do recognise the stamp and I do know Mr. Zrinko Tokic, and this document speaks of this soldier, belonging to the 4th Brigade, was probably born in Gornji Vakuf and that he was killed in fighting in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other HV soldiers killed while they were fighting in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really do not know. This document is dated the 22nd February, 1993. At the time, I couldn't even reach my command in Vitez because I was blocked in Kiseljak. It is possible that they did, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this particular document, a copy of it goes to the welfare coordinator in the Drazevac barracks in Split. Was it the normal practice of the Croatian army to keep records of their soldiers who were killed and wounded?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is the practice of every army to keep records of how they are and whether they are killed or wounded. This applies not only to the Croatian army but to every army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let me show you another document, General, another new document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we are waiting for this document, General, and just a follow-up from my last question concerning records that are kept on the death of soldiers. Is it your experience, General, that as part of this record keeping within the Croatian army and any army, that the army keeps track of where their soldiers were killed, the location of where their soldiers were killed?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't think I've understood your question correctly again. Whether I knew the locality where the soldiers were killed? Is that what you were asking? If so, I'll answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, I'm asking you if, when an army keeps records of where their soldiers were killed, did they also keep records of the geographic location where their soldiers were either killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I didn't specially work on assignments of that type. In Herceg-Bosna and in the HVO, a civilian committee existed for those persons listed missing or killed, and it had standardised forms that were filled out and cooperated with international representatives in that regard. I myself do not know what the form looks like, actually, and how these records are, in fact, kept.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, to your knowledge, did the HV keep that information?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I repeat. I did not work on tasks of that kind. I know that there is a committee for the exchange of missing persons, detainees, and persons killed, and that that committee has its own protocol and standards according to which it functions, but I repeat, I never worked within a commission of that kind and I don't know the records or the forms used in that task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let's move to the document that we have before us. We talked just briefly -- I'm sorry, I didn't get a number on that. I'm sorry, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 601, 601A for the French version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, we talked about just previously the order that Colonel Siljeg issued on the 12th of April asking for the list of HVO officers present in your unit and headquarters, and at 601, we have another document signed by Mr. Zrinko Tokic of the Ante Starcevic Brigade in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: A little slower, please. I just can't follow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will read this document, sir, so you will be able to follow it word by word. This is a document that is dated the 16th of May, 1993, to the 2nd Brigade of the Croatian army. It discusses the "Request to leave your officer, Mate Kunkic, at our disposal in the zone of responsibility of our brigade." "- Given that we are familiar with your plan to withdraw officer Mate Kunkic from this area soon (because of your plans and needs), we ask you not to do so until further notice for the following reasons. "- You know that there is a bitter struggle in these areas (and especially in our brigade's zone of responsibility) for the survival of the Croatian people in these areas and the equality of our people, which can only be achieved through the organisation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and establishment of a province of our people. "- The main battle is being fought against yesterday's allies, who have made the seizing of the living space of the Croats and the expulsion of our population from our homes part of their plans. "- In all the battles so far, each person had their individual place and role, but Mr. Mate Kunkic has traced a special place for himself, initially through the work in the field against the Serbo-Chetnik aggressor from the Kuprek area and recently in the struggle against Muslim forces, which are far more numerous in our territory (in the latest confrontation there were four times more). In the last two confrontations (from 23 November 1992 and from 11 January 1993) until now, when the fourth and decisive confrontation is imminent, Mate Kunkic has been entrusted with the command of the defence of the town and placed at the disposal of other units, and he performed these duties very successfully. Our plans for the future are such that a change would give rise to many new problems, where so far everything has been flowing according to an established schedule of control, command, responsibility, etc. There is no need to say that, since last April, in these areas, he and his Alfa Forse unit have considerably assisted in the organisation of our headquarters and later the brigade. "- Given the above, it is evident why we ask you to leave Mr. Mate Kunkic at our disposal. Believing that you will comply with our request, we thank you and, with the limits of our abilities, we will know how to value your contribution to our impending victory." Signed Zrinko Tokic, Commander of the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade in Gornji Vakuf. So here we have, General, an officer that continued to be an officer in the 2nd Brigade of the Croatian army who has been operating in Gornji Vakuf and in the town of Gornji Vakuf for some significant period of time; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. If you show me a document, then I can see from the document. I said that I did not have information of that kind at the time, nor do I have it now. I don't know about the 2nd Brigade. And it was this officer from this document. I can see a request is being made to the 2nd Brigade that he remains. That is clear from the document. I'd just like to ask, with regard to the first part of your question before you read out the document, you said that Siljeg sent an order to my subordinates and to myself. Siljeg did not send me an order, neither did he send orders to my subordinates. I would like that to be clear because that is the interpretation that I got with regard to the first question that you put.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you were the deputy chief of staff of the entire HVO. You ultimately became the chief of staff of the entire HVO. Is it your testimony that you knew nothing about deployment of HV officers to a town relatively close to your headquarters in Vitez? You knew nothing about any such deployments?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: When, Mr. President? Is it while the witness was the deputy chief of staff of the HVO? That's what referenced in the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's exactly right. He became the chief of staff and the deputy chief of staff. The question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Be very clear about this, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at any time that HV officers fighting in Gornji Vakuf side by side with the HVO in conflict with the Muslims in 1992 and 1993? Did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What period are you talking about? What period are you speaking about? Are you talking about knowledge that the witness would have had at what point?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Any time, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Because after the war he became -- all right. At any time. Very well. Please answer.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I have already answered that I had knowledge after all the events that occurred in 1994 and 1995 but not as to the details, which brigade it was and the details, which officer. Here we're talking about an officer from one of the brigades. They are events that took place in May 1993. In May 1993, I was in the Lasva pocket. Later on I heard about this, but this information was not the subject of my preoccupations. I heard about it later, but not about the details. I'm seeing this document for the first time. I have it in my hands for the first time here today. I did not talk to the author of the document about the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. That's the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, had you heard of Alpha Force?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As to Alpha Force, the Alpha Force that I heard about, I heard about Alpha Force special purpose unit in Operative Zone of Northwest Herzegovina. I heard about that unit earlier on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you hear about them?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, I heard about the unit possibly at the end of 1992, or the beginning of 1993, or in 1993. That's when I heard about that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn at that time that Alpha Force was an HV unit?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know today, Alpha Force was a special purpose unit of the HVO. I don't know that that unit was a unit of the Croatian army. I did not see any documents on that, neither was I ever given information of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let me just put --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll take a break. Do you have another question about this unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just on this particular unit one document, and we can move on, Mr. President, just before the break. It's not a document we're going to question about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Please proceed. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is being handed to you. This is a military information summary of the Cheshire Regiment from the 1st of February, 1993. The operative paragraph is on the bottom of the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 602.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The operative paragraph, Your Honours, is the bottom paragraph which notes from Gornji Vakuf that: "B Company reported that a new group of HVO soldiers were sighted in the Croatian part of town last night. The group referred to as Alpha Force, believed to be approximately 40 in number, were reported to be very well-equipped and motivated." That's the only item at this particular juncture, Mr. President, that we would ask to be read. Of course, this deals with the Gornji Vakuf area. For reference purposes and information, Judge, just as reading this, B Company -- it says "BCOY" in the document. B Company was the company from the Cheshire Regiment that was deployed to Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. We're going to take a 15-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could ask -- if I could possibly get through this area, I think if I could take a 10-minute break or shorter I think I could get through this one particular segment by 1.00. If I can take a shorter break than 15, I think that I can get through a segment of this cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can now resume the hearing. Mr. Kehoe, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. If the witness can be given 406/55, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, you have seen this document before, and this is an order similar to the order issued by Colonel Siljeg, calling for a list of HV officers in your units and your commands; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Colonel Siljeg did not ask for those in my units and commands. He asked for a list of Croatian army officers in his area, that is, the North-western Herzegovina. This order is an order signed by my associate, which is the same in content. It just confirms what I said, that the main staff issued orders to all the commands of the Operative Zones to check out this matter and to make a list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your testimony, General, has been that when you issued this order, there were no HV officers in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That there were no Croatian army officers serving in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, you talked to us, during your direct-examination, about two meetings, one on the 28th of April, and one on the 29th of April, both of whom you have attended with Milivoj Petkovic and Miro Andric. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described, in another portion of your testimony, Miro Andric as a deputy commander of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the number two in the joint command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Speak slowly because the question is a long one and the witness has to be able to assimilate the interpretation. Did you understand the beginning of the question, General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could I be asked question by question, because I have to wait for the interpretation, and I have the impression that the interpreters are having difficulties to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're asking for me to arbitrate here because, of course, it is better to go question by question. On the other hand, if I've understood things correctly, the Prosecutor needs to explain all of this in order to ask his question. It's a little bit complicated. All right. Mr. Kehoe, please try to speak more slowly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Miro Andric represented the HVO with you and Petkovic at these meetings on the 28th of April and the 29th of April; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In what year?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What position did Miro Andric take in the joint command that was set up on the 21st of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In that joint command, HVO officer Miro Andric held the position of deputy commander of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the HVO. Miro Andric was an officer from the main staff of the HVO. I don't know, and I'm not quite sure whether at the time he was also deputy chief of staff of the HVO, but he could have been that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else from the HVO was part of this joint command in addition to Andric?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you give me the order, I would be able to tell you exactly. I know that my representatives were Zivko Totic, Filip Filipovic. I don't know the others in the joint command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina who joined on that day the joint command between the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, from your testimony, General, at least Franjo Nakic -- excuse me. At least Zivko Totic, Filip Filipovic, and Miro Andric were part of this joint command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is right, only we have to make a distinction. There were two joint commands: one at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the joint command of the armed forces, and the commanders were Petkovic and Halilovic. In that joint command, Miro Andric was Petkovic's deputy and members included Filip Filipovic and others. Then another level of the joint command was between the 3rd Corps and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and in that joint command, I was the commander as well as the commander of the 3rd Corps, and our deputies were Franjo Nakic, Dzemo Merdan, and others. So that there were two joint commands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You explained that very well before, and I thank you, on behalf of my colleagues, for having reclarified the situation. Can we move to another question now, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can I turn to a document, Mr. President, and I would like to show the witness 406/17?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this is a document that is dated the 5th of June, 1993 -- excuse me, 1992, I apologise. Signed by the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, and it is sent to the attention of the 101st "R" Brigade and notes: "Pursuant to Article 4, Section 2 of the Decree on the Structure and Strength of the National Guard of the President of the Republic of Croatia, I order: "that the following be sent to the South Front on a temporary basis ..." And the first name on that list is Colonel Miro Andric. We won't read the rest. And it notes that the 101st Brigade will provide equipment and facilities, and there is no need to read all that equipment. And in the last paragraph -- excuse me, the last two paragraphs, it says: "The above-listed members of the Croatian Army shall continue to enjoy all the rights that have so far pertained to them. "The above-mentioned members of the Croatian Army are to report to the Chief of Staff, General Janko Bobetko, in the South Front Command - Ploca." Signed by Gojko Susak. Now let us look at another document, General, and this is a new document, Mr. President. I want you to keep that document with you, please. Excuse me, Mr. Usher. Excuse me, Mr. Usher. If the General could keep that document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 603 and 603A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this is a document that is executed some three days after the previous exhibit. Again, it is on HV stationery for the Croatian army, the date is 8 June 1992, and it is signed on behalf of Colonel Jozo Petrasevic.
