It says: "Pursuant to Point IV, paragraph 2, of the Decision of the President of the Republic of Croatia on the Organisation and Number of Members of the National Guard Corps, and to the Order of 5 June 1992," the number for the previous document, "I hereby issue the following order: "The following men are temporarily assigned to carry out tasks on the southern front, and are hereby sent to the southern front." The first name, Miro Andric, and the same list of individuals, or basically the same list of individuals, plus one, that we discussed in the prior exhibit. Again, in this order from Mr. Petrasevic: "The above-named members of the Croatian Army shall retain all the rights which they have enjoyed and acquired so far. The above-named members of the Croatian Army shall report to General Janko Bobetko in the Command of the Southern Sector - Ploca." General, do you know this individual, this Colonel Jozo Petrasevic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It says on the document "Jozo Petrasevic" and not "Petrecevic" , but in any case, I do not know Colonel Jozo Petrasevic nor have I ever heard of a colonel by that name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise that stamp?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do recognise the stamp. It is the stamp of the military post number -- I can't see the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next document, 406/48. If I can, Mr. Usher, when I discuss this document, after, if we can have 603 available to the General?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 406/48 is a document that is executed on HVO letterhead dated 16 March 1993, directed to army headquarters of -- excuse me, from Army Headquarters of the Croatian Defence Council, and it is directed to the 101st "R" Brigade of the Croatian Army, the personnel department. "At the personal request of Mr. Ivan Zlatanic, Head of the Technical Services of the 2nd Brigade OZ JIH of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, who was transferred to the Southern Battlefield, by order no. ... dated 5 June 1992, of the Republic of Croatia, I hereby agree: "that Mr. Ivan Zlatic, member of the 101st Brigade 'R' of the Croatian Army can return to his original unit. "Mr. Zlatic fulfilled his tasks on the Southern battlefield from (date illegible) until 15 March 1993 and must resolve all pertaining rights and obligations with the 101st 'R' Brigade of the Croatian Army, and has thus to report to the commander of the 101st 'R' Brigade, Colonel Jozo Petrasevic. "I want to note that Mr. Zlatic fulfilled his duties conscientiously and very well, and I, as his superior, am awarding him with 7 (seven) days of leave so that he can resolve all his obligations concerning his position in the 101st Brigade." Signed Deputy Head of Army Command, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna HVO, Miro Andric. Now, General, this is the same Miro Andric that is operating in the joint command and is participating in meetings with you on the 28th and 29th of April, 1993; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this document that I also see for the first time as the previous two, it is said here that Miro Andric is deputy chief of staff of the main staff of the HVO, and that is the Miro Andric who attended the meeting on the 28th and 29th of April, 1993, and who was a member of the command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As I saw the previous two documents for the first time too, it is possible, and I assume that it is the same Miro Andric, but I never spoke to him about these two documents as I had never seen them before anyway, and they apply to the period of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in document 4 -- in document 406/48, which, in fact, is dated 16 March, 1993, it discusses a Mr. Ivan Zlatanic. Now, that is the same name that is on 603, the same Ivan -- or appears to be the same name without an "N," excuse me. Does that appear to be the same man?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It could be, yes. Under number 4, it says Ivan Zlatic, and here too it's Ivan Zlatic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So reading these two documents together, we have these soldiers from the 101st "R" Brigade deployed to, at least one, deployed to Bosnia-Herzegovina from at least June of 1992 to the 16th of March of 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is right because, according to document 603, this group is being sent to the southern front to report to the commander of the southern front, General Janko Bobetko, and where General Janko Bobetko will send them to when they reported to him, I don't know, and from this document, 406/48, it can be seen that they were included in the Operative Zone of the Southeastern Herzegovina of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were any of them sent to the Central Bosnian Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you another document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 604 and 604A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let us read this document. Upper left-hand corner: "HVO main staff. Colonel Miro Andric. Vitez. 3 May, 1993." It is directed to the 101st Croatian Army Brigade with a fax number, with a report: "The below mentioned servicemen of the 101st HV Brigade who are at the southern front of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna pursuant to an order of the Republic of Croatia Ministry of Defence are performing the same duties as they performed in March." The names: "1. Colonel Miro Andric. 2. Blaz Andric. 3. Mirsad Sivac. 4. Branko Kozul. 5. Major Goran Vujic. The servicemen were on duty for 30 days in April. Colonel Miro Andric." It is stamped with the Central Bosnia Operative Zone stamp from Travnik. Is that your stamp, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The stamp is, but since the formation of the joint command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Colonel Miro Andric and his associates stayed in Zenica or Vitez and the joint command did not have its own stamp. I believe that he occasionally did the stamp of the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, but he was stationed as a representative of the joint command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The agreement was they should be stationed for a period in Zenica and then for a period in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, let us look at these names that are in 604 and compare them to the list of 603. I ask you to look at the names in 603, 9, 10, and 11. Mirsad Sicvic, Blaz Andric, and Branko Kozul. In addition to Miro Andric, these members of the Croatian army are the same men that are mentioned in both documents; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, clearly. These were the drivers of the Colonel and the deputy commander of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Branko Kozul is a private, Blaz Andric has a driver and that was his escort. This escort was captured by the 7th Muslim Brigade at Ravno Rostovo, where it is travelling officially towards Bugojno. I repeat, these are commanders of the joint command of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina appointed on the basis of a joint agreement, and that meeting was chaired by Mr. Thebault. I am not sure that General Morillon was there. They are not officers of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, the Operative Zone of which I was the commander. Never was any one of them an officer in the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it clear to you, General, after reviewing these documents that there were, in fact, soldiers and officers from the Croatian army operating and working in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the HVO in Southeastern Herzegovina and not Western Herzegovina, it is clear to me, but I still stick to what I said and assert that there were never officers from the Croatian army operating in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, neither officers nor soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when Miro Andric was operating in Central Bosnia and attending meetings with you, was he wearing an HVO insignia or an HV insignia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I met Miro Andric regarding the duty he performed, deputy chief of staff of the HVO. We met for the first time at a meeting in Zenica on the 28th of April, 1993, when the joint command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina was formed. At that time he wore HVO insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, when did you first learn that Miro Andric was a member of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When he was a member of the Croatian army, would you tell me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, General, my question is this: When did you first learn that Miro Andric was an officer in the Croatian army this entire time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That Miro Andric, prior to taking the position of deputy chief of staff of the HVO was a member of the Croatian army, it is something that I learned today, but I learned before this that after serving in the HVO he went to the HV, but until today I believed that he had started his military career in the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did Miro Andric go after he left the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: After he left the HVO, he went to the Defence Ministry. I don't know whether that was his first assignment but, in any event, he went to the Croatian army. Towards the end of 1995, in December, I knew that he was working as an officer in the Defence Ministry of the Republic of Croatia. This same Miro Andric, who on the 28th of April, 1993, that I saw for the first time in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it strike you, General, that when you saw and found out that Miro Andric was back in Zagreb working for the Ministry of Defence and was part of the Croatian army, that he was, in fact, a Croatian army officer in Central Bosnia in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was not an officer of the Croatian army in Central Bosnia in April 1993. He was an officer from the main staff of the HVO and in the joint command of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, according to what I knew then. Today, I see from this document that for a time he was a member of the Croatian army before he joined the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, looking at 604, looking at document 604, the order written in Vitez, where your headquarters was, on the 3rd of May, 1993, it indicates that these servicemen were and continue to be a part of the Croatian army; doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is not an order, it is just a note, a memorandum. I see this information today, that they spent 30 days on duty, and the document was signed by Miro Andric as deputy chief of staff of the main staff, and I have already said that I didn't know that he had been a member of the Croatian army before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this report indicate to you, General, that these soldiers, at the time this report was written on the 3rd of May, 1993, were still members of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From this report, one could conclude that they were members of the Croatian army, but I have already said that the joint command used the stamp and the joint command was based in Zenica and Travnik, so that I did not stay in the joint command. They wrote out the documents. What was addressed to me was sent to me and the others were sent to other people, where they wanted to send them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. You've been very helpful on this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I might consult with my colleagues for one moment, I think that it might -- Mr. President, I realise I've run over 1.00. We are going to move into another area. Given the fact that it's lunchtime, I --

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If I may be allowed, Mr. President, may I just add regarding document 604 that the heading is, "The main staff of the HVO," and the town of Vitez, and not the command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, as far as this document is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. That's been indicated. Let me remind you that ordinarily this afternoon we would be having an ex parte hearing. Therefore, I don't really know -- Mr. Kehoe, you're not going to be conducting your cross-examination this afternoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I think that my colleague, Mr. Harmon, has the matter that's before the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Did you want to speak about it right away, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President and Your Honours, not at all. I'll be in Court at the Court's request this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We've run overtime a little bit. I know that the interpreters have to rest up. We won't be in before quarter to three. Let's say quarter to three. Mr. Registrar, tell anybody who should be told.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. This hearing will resume at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.
